Repo /home/user/VTT. You own ONLY: scripts/authoring/krezk_land.py, krezk-village.py, krezk-abbey.py, app/src/kit/sites/s.ts and the generated locations/ch08/S/** and locations/ch08/S10/**. Do not edit any other file (backdrop.ts, materials.ts, surfaces.ts, world.json, heightfield.py are being changed in parallel by other clusters); if you need something there, say so in your final report. Run scripts from the repo root with python3 (krezk-village.py, then krezk-abbey.py, which imports krezk_land). Typecheck the app with `npm run typecheck` at the repo root; `npm run preview` serves :4173 (one may already be running). Screenshots: a Playwright harness exists at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-VTT/3e57a1ac-07da-5111-aa9e-cccc471b7481/scratchpad/smooth/audit/shoot.cjs (reuse or write your own).

GOAL (the user's words): in Krezk the mountain looks all open and the trail to the abbey is practically vertical; make the world's logic hold and things feel real. Favour realism over the book's literal 400 ft: keep '400 ft above the village' only as a DM-note string (S5/S7 notes in krezk-village.py and krezk-abbey.py).

MEASURED NOW: krezk_land.py LEDGE = 400, MOUNT_RISE = 320; ROAD (chaikin of ROAD_PTS) is 651-725 ft long for a 400-ft rise, each leg 55-61% grade (~30 deg). ground() makes a mesa: profiles from the rim centre W 400,400,400,348,55,0 and N 400,431,426,379,203,67,0 (74-82 deg faces, _cliff_k = 6 ft/ft); only the NE rises (to 675-695 in frame). krezk-village.py taper() scales the heightfield to 15% within 320 ft of the lattice edge (lattice x 330..1160, z -430..650), so the mountain is a lone dome ringed by flat forest. s.ts heightfield() colours steep faces by `floor((y + 6 sin(x*0.045) + 5 cos(z*0.06)) / 18) % 3` into ROCK_DK/ROCK/ROCK_MID, which reads as horizontal zig-zag stripes at every distance; its materials are single-sided (camera inside the mass sees through it). tower-e (565,0,536) stands where the land is 34 ft; pine-m235/253/259 are sunk 33/9/2.7 ft (y sampled with KL.slope_at before taper). 2,211 pines (forest 20/26-ft spacing, 17 ft inside the walls) hide the cottages. s.ts declares CHAIN = '#5a5d63' as metal, which is PALETTE.mist3 (stone) and recolours 244 gravestones/33 statues/church walls on E, N, U, Z with the iron grain; SACK '#a8956f' collides with a wood declaration. krezk-abbey.py line 27 hard-codes LEDGE = 400 with levels 400/415/420/380 (loft 420 is inside upper's 415-423).

REGION CONTEXT (read-only, locations/ch02/barovia-region/world.json; sample with the same bilinear scheme as app/src/core/terrain.ts, backdrop draws it x1.25): pin S at ~420-440 ft; today the rows rise only W/NW (460-570 at 0.5-0.75 mi) and fall NE/E/S. The 'region' cluster is adding a ridge N/NE of Krezk so rows read ~650-760 ft at 0.75-1.25 mi NE of the pin. The 'backdrop' cluster is making backdrop.ts continue the map's own edge height into the land beyond (today it flattens to the village elevation within 900 ft). Build to meet both: your lattice edge heights should go toward the region x1.25 height at that point (sampled from world.json at run time), NOT toward 0.

DO:
1. krezk_land.py: LEDGE -> ~230 (200-250). Rebuild ROAD_PTS as three (or more) switchback legs totalling >= 1,050 ft so no segment exceeds 22% (compute and print the max grade; target 20-22%): e.g. first leg from the foot by the S3 lane (~(452,447)) north ~380 ft along the whole west face (extend SZ to z 150-470), hairpin, ~380 ft back south, hairpin, ~330 ft north to the rim; re-derive LEG_APEX, LEGS, _benches, and the lk-switchback link positions in krezk-village.py. Keep heightfield_dims()/ribbon_dims() output format unchanged (nx, nz, cell, q, d#, frost, skirt, drop; you may ADD optional keys) because yester-hill.py copies this encoder and s.ts heightfield() is also used by Yester Hill.
2. krezk-village.py: replace taper() with a blend toward the region height at the lattice edge; set tower-e's y (and every mountainside pine's y) from the same hf_fn+taper the heightfield uses; in-wall tree spacing 17 -> 24 ft with 14 ft clear along each cottage's long sides and 8 ft along lanes (near_road(p, 8)); forest spacing 20/26 -> 24/32 ft. Keep 'about 400 ft' as the DM note.
3. krezk-abbey.py: LEDGE = KL.LEDGE, derive all level elevations from it (ground/upper/loft/cellar), fix loft stacking (loft at the upper ceiling or upper ceilingFt 5), keep the valley level's FOOT where the road starts, make the ~70 valley cottages/towers static props (vis 'player', no size) so build.ts merges them. Regenerate S then S10.
4. s.ts heightfield(): drop the %3 band colouring; colour steep faces (k < 0.62) by plan-space value noise (same idea as krezk_land.rugged/noise, ~22-ft cells) and the face normal's azimuth: ROCK on ribs, ROCK_DK on flanks facing away from the key light (the sun is roughly south-east: see World.key in app/src/render/world.ts), ROCK_MID on gully floors; a thin SCREE band only within ~12 ft of a face's local foot; mid slopes scree, gentle turf/frost as now. Build with matClone(color) and side THREE.DoubleSide. Make sure every colour used (ROCK, ROCK_DK, ROCK_MID, SCREE, FROST, turf) has a surfaceFor() declaration with the right material (rock, rock, rock, rubble or dirt, snow, grass) and unique hexes. CHAIN -> own hex (e.g. '#55585e') in the metal list; SACK -> own hex kept as cloth. Share one module-level mist material in mistBank (patchFog'd, from materials.ts helpers) instead of a new MeshBasicMaterial per bank. Cheap nit: woodpile as one box body plus a single merged log-ends geometry tagged userData.tier='near'.

VERIFY: print road length and max grade (<= 22%), max/min heightfield heights at the lattice edge vs region x1.25 at those points (difference < 30 ft), tower/pine y vs ground (|dy| < 1 ft); `npm run typecheck`; `npm test` if scene tests exist; screenshots of S from the tabletop default, from the east at ~900 ft (no dome on a plain, no stripes), the road foot, and S10's valley level. review.summary:
Verdict: fail. Seven of the eight issues check out. The plug-to-mountainside block fix only works inside the frame: a new wall about 450 ft high now stands at the N and E frame edges, and you see it whenever you zoom out from Krezk. That ties directly to the user's complaint that zoom in / zoom out nesting is not working as intended.

Setup: worktree HEAD is 966a0f2b; I modified no files. The diff against 6a8324d touches only the 6 allowed paths (krezk_land.py, krezk-village.py, krezk-abbey.py, s.ts, ch08/S and ch08/S10 scene.json). I rebuilt dist because it was older than the commit, and the build is clean. vitest passed 155/155 on one run; on two other runs one test failed, tests/bestiary.test.ts, with a 5 s timeout under machine load. That test has nothing to do with this cluster. audit-outdoor.py reports nothing for S or S10, and its output is identical to main.

Confirmed fixed:
1. Switchback road (block): measured from the regenerated S5-road ribbon, it runs 910 ft of plan length for a 199.4-ft rise. The average grade is 21.9%, the steepest single segment is 22.2%, and the steepest 30-ft window is 21.9%. Legs are 410/289/211 ft. LEDGE is 200 rather than the suggested 230; the fixer's reason is that three legs fit on the west face. In S-westface.png the benches and hairpins sit on shelves.
2. Cliff colouring and sidedness (fix): the 18-ft height bands are gone; faces are coloured by noise and light direction instead (S-westface.png, S-cliff-close.png). At runtime every land material has side = 2 (DoubleSide), and rugged() uses an amplitude of 30.
3. S10 levels (fix): ground 200, upper 215, loft 223 (the upper floor's ceiling), cellar 180. Hall walls are 23 ft, and the S10 valley ceiling is 198.
4. Tower and pines (fix): in a lattice_sampler check of every S village object, only 4 are off the ground: S4-rock3, the S1 signpost, and the two low-mist banks (the fixer's note says the low-mist bank floats by design). tower-e and tower-ne stand on the village floor. Mountain pines sit on the land.
5. Hex collisions (fix): '#55585e' and '#aa9670' now appear only in s.ts. At runtime the surface codes read rock 16 for ROCK/ROCK_DK/ROCK_MID, rubble 3 for SCREE and snow 18 for FROST.
6. Pines (fix): 166 village, 429 forest and 1444 mountain pines (2039 in total, down from 2211). No pine stands within 14 ft of a cottage centre. Spacing is 24 ft in the walls and 24/32 ft in the forest, and cottages read clearly in S-default.png.
7. Nit: mist banks share one material per opacity (2 materials at runtime), and the woodpile is a box plus a merged mesh of log ends.

Not fixed (block issue #2): the ledge is a real shelf on a mountainside in the close views. WHAT IS WRONG (measured):
1. backdrop.ts yAt() (~line 90) flattens the land to the level's elevation: `yTop + (h - yTop) * smooth(120, 900, d)`. Consequences: Krezk (ch08/S) has its own 'heightfield' prop reaching 485 ft at the NE corner while the backdrop 900 ft beyond is at -138; Tsolenka (ch09/T) cuts a 420-ft gorge that ends at the map edge against land at -0.4; Berez (ch10/U) meets +963 ft within 900 ft SE, Old Bonegrinder (ch06/O) +439 at 2,640 ft E, the Amber Temple (ch13/X) +671 at 900 ft SE with the road ribbon rising at ~60 deg. FIX: in app.ts after buildLevel, raycast the built level (floors AND land props; use the built group's bounding box, which for Krezk is the heightfield lattice x 330..1160, z -430..650, not just the floor polygons) at ~64 points per side, plus a fallback to the level's elevation where nothing is hit, and pass `edgeHeights` (or an edgeY(x,z) sampler) to buildBackdrop. In yAt(): edge = interpolated nearest edge sample; grade cap h' = edge + clamp(h - edge, -0.25*d, +0.25*d) for the first 2,000 ft; return edge + (h' - edge) * smooth(120, 900, d). Keep the castle crag/pillar logic for K working. The 'krezk' cluster is rebuilding its mountain so the lattice edge meets the region x1.25 height, and the 'region' cluster is raising world.json rows NE of Krezk, so with this change the land will continue smoothly; the 'yester-wines' cluster adds a heightfield dome to ch14/Y which also relies on it.
2. Interiors buried (block): app.ts buildBackdrop takes the elevation from the first level with terrain, and the land is flush at yTop-0.4 over the whole map footprint, so the Amber Temple's upper (+30) and lower (0) levels render as a white snow plane with floating labels (shots x-tabletop-upper/lower.png), and N4/U/W cellars 10-12 ft under their open-air level get the same. FIX in setLevel(): when the current level has no terrain and elevationFt < l0.elevationFt - 1, hide backdrop.getObjectByName('land') (and mist rings) for that level, and/or in yAt() return min(level elevations) - 3 inside the footprint (mapDist == 0) or cut a hole over bounds padded ~10 ft. Related: backdrop.ts line ~176 `if (crag > 0 && !HF)` skips the crag pillar whenever a heightfield exists, so Castle Ravenloft's dungeon/larder boxes (-40/-80 ft) hang in open air with grass behind them (shots-k ch04_K__ground.png). Draw a rock plinth under the map bounds from yTop-2 down to yAt() when HF && crag > 0, and the same plinth for any stacked scene whose minimum level elevation is below the backdrop ground (Death House dungeon, N4 cellar, W cellar, X).
3. Grain missing: (a) context level materials (app.ts ~line 917) are cloned with mm.clone(); three r180 Material.copy() does not carry onBeforeCompile/customProgramCacheKey but DOES copy userData.mist=true, so the clone is a bare Lambert and patchFog no-ops: 57k tris of '#211d1f' context with no surface and never fogged on every area map. Build the context material with matClone('#'+src.color.getHexString(), true) then lerp its colour toward the mist, or after cloning `delete k.userData.mist; setSurface(k, surfaceOf(hex)); patchFog(k, true)`. (b) Token figures (app.ts ~541, 'tokens are never fogged') are rebuilt with bare `new THREE.MeshLambertMaterial(...)`: keep the private material but call setSurface(m, surfaceOf(hex)); patchFog(m, true) (exempt=true keeps them unfogged).
4. Backdrop debloat (backdrop.ts): ribbon() (~442-459) makes one Mesh + new MeshBasicMaterial per road/river (74-100 meshes, 43-56k tris per outdoor map; unlit so they ignore day/night; ungrained; a village's grey cobble road turns into a bright tan ribbon at the map edge, e-village-horizon.png). Accumulate all roads into one geometry and all rivers into another, MeshLambertMaterial({vertexColors:true, flatShading:true}) with setSurface 'dirt' (rivers 'water') and patchFog(m, true); seed the first segment's colour from the FLOOR_COLOR of the map road it leaves (exitFor()). Also sample ribbon heights along the heightfield at intermediate points and, when a segment's grade exceeds 25%, insert switchback points instead of a straight climb. The instanced forest (lines ~192-207) submits n = 9500 with dropped trees as zero-scale matrices: write only kept trees and set trees.count = kept. hazed() (line ~59) bakes a distance colour per site material so collapse() cannot merge sites: bake haze into a vertex colour attribute and use one vertexColors Lambert per surface so the ~85-117 backdrop meshes collapse to a few. The settlement/landmark shadow discs (line ~406, '#2d3332' etc.) are MeshBasic and ignore night: lambert(blend(...)) with patchFog exempt, or drop them on heightfield maps.
5. app.ts applySlider(): on non-stacked maps `o.userData.cap -> visible = !lowWalls` hides EVERY roof cap, so the N8 square's four shops and N7/N5 stand roofless beside roofed context houses. Hide a cap only when the party token (or the selected room) is inside that cap's building footprint; otherwise keep caps and clip walls only.

Radius R = half extent + 450 ft draws 158-176 houses round a 70x55 shop (Blinsky's 232k tris, church as N1 221k vs 5k as E5): use 250 ft for interiors (450 only for placement maps) and drop pines/stumps beyond 150 ft. In setLevel() for stacked sites keep PointLights visible only for the current level and the one directly above/below (or the 12 nearest the camera target). Lights of the floor you look at stay as authored.
8. gridOverlay.ts buildGridOverlay(): for ground=false the grid is one plane over the bbox (pad 1.5), so lines hang in the air beside octagon towers (wsc/03-compound L3), across the abbey courtyard at the wall-walk height (S10 upper), Argynvostholt's roof terrace and the Z8 shelf. Build from the union of g.floorPolygons (one plane per polygon, or a coverage mask in the shader).
